clue.text: She can't get to work unless someone lends her a hand

definitions.text: She can't get to work unless someone lends her a hand

parts.words: She can't get to work unless someone lends her a hand
parts.note: lending a hand sounds like helping out, but here a client literally offers a hand to be groomed

explanation.surface: A woman who needs help from others before she can do her job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lends her a hand' reads as giving help; literally, the customer holds out a hand for nail care.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail technician can only work once a client presents a hand for filing and polishing.

clue.text: Frenzied cablegram to reassure worried relatives?

definitions.meaning: wild and out of control, running riot
a terse telegram saying 'I am fine' would be clipped to two short words

explanation.surface: A frantic telegram sent home to calm anxious family members.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AM OK: the shortest possible telegram telling the family all is well.
explanation.definitionFit: Running wild in a frenzy is the standard sense; the second reading is the telegram phrase.

clue.text: Carries out a grave commitment

parts.note: a grave commitment sounds like a serious pledge, but it means committing a body to the grave

explanation.surface: Someone fulfils a serious promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like 'serious'; it is the burial plot.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body is to consign it to the grave, a solemn commitment.

clue.text: Spenser heroine given articles of merchandise in the dark?

parts.note: Una is the heroine of Book I of Spenser's poem The Faerie Queene
ware means goods for sale, as in hardware or earthenware

explanation.surface: A poetic heroine is handed a load of goods in the darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: Una is the virtuous lady of Edmund Spenser's Elizabethan epic The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: Being kept in the dark means being ignorant of what is happening.

clue.text: It holds nothing over a minor classical character

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sits over the next, so it comes first
the word It holds something within it, so it is the container for the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Something sits above an unimportant figure from the ancient world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor classical character' is a small Greek letter, and also a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the ninth and smallest letter of the Greek alphabet, so a minor character of classical Greek.

clue.text: Terrible agony or utter chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so the preceding letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Dreadful pain, or else complete disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chaos' looks like part of the surface list; it is the anagram signal on OR UTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment of extreme pain is terrible agony.

clue.text: The great brain behind a much acclaimed quizshow?

definitions.meaning: the planner who ... a scheme from behind the scenes
a famous BBC television quiz with its black chair

explanation.surface: The genius behind a celebrated television quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: Mastermind is a long-running BBC quiz in which contestants sit in a black chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain behind a plot is its planner; the same name belongs to a well-known British quiz programme.

clue.text: Craftsman whose work may well be of monumental importance

definitions.text: Craftsman whose work may well be of monumental importance

parts.words: Craftsman whose work may well be of monumental importance
parts.note: monumental importance sounds like great significance, but literally means carving monuments such as headstones

explanation.surface: A skilled worker whose output matters enormously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monumental' means huge in the surface; literally it is about memorials and gravestones.
explanation.definitionFit: A carver of stone makes monuments and headstones.

clue.text: What every cobbler will have to endure

definitions.meaning: a shoemaker's foot-shaped block used to shape footwear
to go on, survive, hold out

explanation.surface: Every shoemaker has something to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: A cobbler's last is the wooden foot model on which shoes are made or mended.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler shapes shoes on a wooden foot form; to endure is to keep going.

clue.text: Correspondence college tutor who handles lots of mail?

parts.note: post means letters and correspondence
a master is a teacher at a school or college

explanation.surface: A teacher at a correspondence college deals with a heap of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the one who handles lots of mail, the head of a post office.
explanation.definitionFit: The official in charge of a post office deals with large quantities of letters.

clue.text: One of Neptune's main attendants

parts.note: main means the sea here, so an attendant of the sea god, not a chief one

explanation.surface: A leading member of the sea god's retinue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'chief', but is the old word for the sea; this sea-god merman was a son of Neptune's Greek counterpart.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth this merman blowing a conch shell attends the sea god.

clue.text: Rash and tumultuous parliamentary record

indicators.note: tumultuous means disorderly and turbulent, so the letters are thrown about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A hasty and riotous account of proceedings in parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The official verbatim report of UK parliamentary debates is named after printer Luke Hansard.
explanation.definitionFit: The official printed transcript of debates in the British Parliament bears this name.

clue.text: Servant-girl who operates as a 1,maybe

definitions.meaning: 1 across, a nail technician, works on hands and may be a young woman

explanation.surface: A maid who works like the beautician at 1 across.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as HAND MAIDEN: the nail technician of 1 across is a young woman who works on hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A female servant or attendant is the traditional sense; the second reading splits it into hand plus young woman.

clue.text: Italian city man bundled into a plane?

indicators.note: bundled means pushed roughly, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man from Italy is pushed onto an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of INTO A PLANE gives a native of Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Naples, the southern Italian city, takes this name.

clue.text: Last place one would expect public transport to go to

definitions.text: Last place one would expect public transport to go to

parts.words: Last place one would expect public transport to go to
parts.note: sounds like an unlikely destination, but means the final stop where buses are garaged

explanation.surface: Somewhere buses would never be expected to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last place one would expect' suggests unlikely; literally it is the final stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Buses end their day at the garage where vehicles are kept.

clue.text: Coarse fabric produced by sheepish male after watered down spirit

indicators.note: after places the sheep piece behind the spirit piece

parts.note: grog is rum diluted with water, as served to sailors
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: Rough cloth made by a bashful man after diluted liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' means bashful on the surface but is literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse cloth of silk, mohair and wool was once used for cloaks.

clue.text: "God loveth a cheerful ——" (II Corinthians)

parts.note: a quotation from Paul's second letter to the Corinthians, chapter 9, with the last word missing

explanation.surface: A biblical line with its final word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: 2 Corinthians 9:7 in the King James Version.
explanation.definitionFit: The verse praises one who gives donations willingly and gladly.

clue.text: Uncanny point I have gone into before

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

indicators.note: gone into means the I letter has entered the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something weird slipped in at an earlier moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and unsettling, weird or spooky.

clue.text: Niggardly approach

explanation.surface: A stingy way of drawing close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' meaning tight-fisted is chiefly British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy is an old sense of the word; to come closer is the everyday one.

clue.text: Lack of objectivity I find among arts graduates

indicators.note: among places the I inside the graduates

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is an arts degree, so BAS are its holders
taken as written

explanation.surface: I detect prejudice among humanities degree-holders.
explanation.definitionFit: Prejudice or partiality is a lack of objectivity.

clue.text: Remedial measures

parts.note: sounds like corrective steps, but means measured quantities of medicine

explanation.surface: Steps taken to put something right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measures' suggests actions; here they are quantities of a remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Prescribed quantities of medicine are amounts that heal.

clue.text: Red card for the baseball player?

definitions.meaning: a playing card in one of the two red suits
the infield of a baseball ground, shaped like a rhombus

explanation.surface: A sending-off for a baseball player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red card' suggests a football sending-off; it is a playing card of a red suit.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the red suits in a pack of cards shares its name with the baseball infield.

clue.text: Militant miners?

parts.note: sounds like strike-happy coal workers, but means soldiers who dig tunnels

explanation.surface: Coal workers spoiling for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Militant' suggests union activism; literally it is military engineers who dig saps and mines.
explanation.definitionFit: Military engineers who dig trenches and lay mines, especially Royal Engineers.

clue.text: Enlightened by Cynthia overnight?

parts.note: Cynthia is a name of the moon goddess Artemis, so lit by her at night

explanation.surface: Someone suddenly understanding things thanks to a woman friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cynthia' looks like a friend's name; it is a poetic name for the moon goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Lit up at night by the light of the lunar goddess.

clue.text: No time to get a light meal in Araby

definitions.text: No time to get a light meal in Araby

parts.words: No time to get a light meal in Araby
parts.note: a period when Muslims eat nothing during daylight hours

explanation.surface: No chance for a snack in Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light meal' suggests a snack; it is any meal taken in daylight during the fasting month.
explanation.definitionFit: The Islamic holy month of fasting forbids eating from dawn to sunset.

clue.text: First letter opened by a Philistine city girl

indicators.note: opened by means the letter piece is preceded by the other pieces

parts.note: Gath was one of the five Philistine cities in the Bible, home of Goliath
A is the first letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An initial letter is unsealed by a girl from an ancient biblical city.
explanation.walkthrough: Gath, birthplace of Goliath, is the Philistine city.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, as in the crime writer Christie.

clue.text: I'm about to stay in the same place

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two letters go round the word for stay

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
to bide is to stay or wait

explanation.surface: Someone is planning to remain where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'going to'; 'about' is the container and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'in the same place', used in references to cite the work just quoted.

clue.text: Not a full-sized horse pistol

explanation.surface: A small horse pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: A horse pistol was a large holster pistol; the surface uses the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A young male horse; also a revolver made by Samuel Colt's firm.

clue.text: Pot-plant?

parts.note: sounds like a houseplant in a pot, but means the plant from which pot, cannabis, comes

explanation.surface: A plant grown in a flowerpot.
explanation.walkthrough: Pot is slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is the plant that yields the drug and also rope fibre.

clue.text: Eager to take part in a ballet?

definitions.meaning: keen and alert, ready for action

definitions.text: to take part in a ballet?
definitions.meaning: ballerinas dance balanced on the tips of the feet

explanation.surface: Keen to dance in a ballet.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for alert and eager is also the literal position of a dancer en pointe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means alert and ready; literally it describes dancing en pointe.

clue.text: A test of brevity

parts.note: sounds like a test of being brief, but means a test whose name is a shortened word

explanation.surface: A test of how concisely one can express things.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself an abbreviation of a longer word for a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of 'examination', a test.

clue.text: Their impressions vary from day to day

definitions.text: Their impressions vary from day to day

parts.words: Their impressions vary from day to day
parts.note: impressions suggests opinions, but means the inked marks a rubber stamp makes, changing daily

explanation.surface: People whose opinions change every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressions' looks like opinions; it is printed marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubber stamps that print the day's date are adjusted every day.
